easy.def: To cover by folding something around.
examples: Wrap the gift.
She wrapped the baby.
He wraps the sandwich.

more.def: To cover something by putting paper or cloth around it.
examples: Wrap the present in colorful paper.
She wrapped the baby in a blanket.
He wrapped the sandwich in foil.

easy.def: The paper or plastic that covers a food or a gift.
examples: I threw away the wrapper.
The candy wrapper is red.
Take off the wrapper.

more.def: A piece of paper, foil or plastic that is wrapped around something, such as candy or a gift.
examples: I peeled the wrapper off the candy bar and threw it in the trash.
The gift wrapper was covered in stars.
Please put your wrapper in the bin.

easy.def: Very strong anger.
examples: The king's wrath was great.
The wrath of the storm.
She felt wrath.

more.def: Great anger, especially in old stories and writing.
examples: The king's wrath shook the whole castle.
The village feared the wrath of the angry giant.
He felt wrath at the sight of the broken window.

easy.def: A ring of leaves or flowers.
examples: We hung a wreath on the door.
The wreath is green.
A wreath of flowers sat on the table.

more.def: A ring made of leaves, flowers or branches, used for decoration.
examples: A green wreath hung on the front door at winter.
She made a wreath from daisies.
The winner wore a wreath of leaves in the old story.

easy.def: Something that is badly broken or destroyed.
examples: The old car was a wreck.
The ship was a wreck at the bottom of the sea.
The kitchen was a wreck after we cooked.

more.def: Something that has been badly broken, such as a ship or car, or a person who is very messy or tired.
examples: Divers found a wreck at the bottom of the sea.
The old car was a wreck and would not start.
The kitchen was a wreck after the party.

easy.def: To break or ruin something.
examples: The storm wrecked the fence.
The wind wrecked our tent.
I wrecked my bike.

more.def: To break something so badly that it cannot be used.
examples: The storm wrecked the old shed.
The waves wrecked the little boat on the rocks.
He wrecked his toy by dropping it down the stairs.

easy.def: The broken pieces left after something is badly damaged.
examples: The wreckage lay on the beach.
We saw the wreckage of the ship.
Wreckage floated by.

more.def: The broken pieces of something that has been badly damaged or destroyed.
examples: Pieces of wreckage from the old ship washed up on the beach.
Workers cleared the wreckage from the road after the storm.
Divers explored the wreckage of the sunken boat.

easy.def: A tool for turning nuts and bolts.
examples: Dad used a wrench.
The wrench is in the toolbox.
I need a wrench to fix the bike.

more.def: A metal tool with a gripping end used to turn nuts and bolts.
examples: Dad used a wrench to tighten the bolt on my bike.
The plumber took a big wrench out of her toolbox.
He turned the wrench until the nut came loose.

easy.def: To pull or twist something hard.
examples: He wrenched the lid off the jar.
She wrenched her ankle.
I wrenched the door open.

more.def: To pull or twist something suddenly and with force.
examples: He wrenched the jar lid open with both hands.
She wrenched her ankle on the uneven path.
The wind wrenched the umbrella out of her hand.

easy.def: To hold and push someone down, as a sport.
examples: The boys wrestle on the mat.
I wrestled with my brother.
They wrestle for fun.

more.def: To fight with someone by holding and pushing, as a sport; or to struggle hard with something.
examples: The two teammates wrestled for fun on the soft mat.
He wrestled with the heavy suitcase until he got it up the stairs.
I wrestled with the hard math problem for an hour.

easy.def: A person who does a sport where two people hold each other down.
examples: The wrestler is strong.
My brother is a wrestler.
The wrestler won the match.

more.def: A person who takes part in the sport of wrestling, in which two people try to push or hold each other down on a mat.
examples: My brother is a wrestler on the high school team.
The wrestler practiced his moves on the mat.
Wrestlers are matched against others of the same weight.

easy.def: A sport where two people try to pin each other.
examples: He likes wrestling.
Wrestling is a sport.
My brother is on the wrestling team.

more.def: A sport in which two people try to hold each other down on a mat.
examples: He joined the wrestling team at school.
Wrestling takes strength and balance.
The wrestling match lasted three rounds.

easy.def: A very sad and unlucky person.
examples: The poor wretch was cold.
He felt like a wretch.
A wretch in the story.

more.def: A very unhappy or unlucky person who is felt to deserve pity.
examples: The poor wretch in the story had no shoes and no home.
He felt like a wretch after he lost the game.
The kind woman gave the wretch some bread.

easy.def: Very sad, poor or bad.
examples: The wretched puppy was cold.
I felt wretched.
It was a wretched day.

more.def: Very unhappy, miserable or of very poor quality.
examples: The wretched puppy shivered in the cold.
I felt wretched after I broke my friend's toy.
The weather was wretched, so we stayed inside.

easy.def: To twist and squeeze to get water out.
examples: Wring out the towel.
I wrung the cloth.
She wrung out her shirt.

more.def: To twist and squeeze something wet in order to force the water out.
examples: I wrung out the wet towel and hung it up.
She wrung the water out of her shirt after the rain.
Dad wrung the mop over the bucket.

easy.def: A small line or fold in skin or cloth.
examples: My shirt has a wrinkle.
Grandpa has wrinkles by his eyes.
I smooth the wrinkle in the paper.

more.def: A small line or fold in skin, cloth, or paper.
examples: She ironed the shirt to take out the wrinkles.
The map had deep wrinkles from being folded.
Laughing makes little wrinkles appear around her eyes.

easy.def: Full of small folds or lines.
examples: My shirt is wrinkled.
Wrinkled skin.
A wrinkled paper.

more.def: Having small lines or folds, as in cloth or skin.
examples: My shirt was wrinkled after I took it out of the bag.
The old man had a kind, wrinkled face.
The wrinkled paper was smoothed flat.

easy.def: The joint where your hand joins your arm.
examples: I wear a watch on my wrist.
My wrist hurts.
She twisted her wrist.

more.def: The narrow part of your arm where it joins your hand.
examples: A bracelet circled her wrist.
She hurt her wrist when she fell.
He flicked his wrist to throw the ball.

easy.def: A small clock that you wear on your arm.
examples: Dad wears a wristwatch.
My wristwatch tells the time.
I got a wristwatch.

more.def: A small watch worn on the wrist.
examples: Dad looked at his wristwatch to check the time.
She got a blue wristwatch for her birthday.
His wristwatch has a loud alarm.

easy.def: To make letters and words with a pencil or pen.
examples: I write my name.
She wrote a note.
Write the word here.

more.def: To put words or numbers on paper, or on a screen, using a pen or keyboard.
examples: Please write your name at the top of the page.
She wrote a letter to her grandfather.
He is writing a story about a pirate.

easy.def: A person who writes.
examples: She is a writer.
The writer wrote a book.
My mom is a writer.

more.def: A person who writes stories, articles or books.
examples: The writer signed her new book.
My aunt is a writer for a newspaper.
The writer spent a year on the story.

easy.def: Words that someone puts on paper.
examples: Your writing is neat.
I like writing stories.
The writing on the sign is big.

more.def: Words that someone has written, or the activity of putting words on paper.
examples: Her writing is neat and easy to read.
The class practices writing every day.
The writing on the old note had faded.

easy.def: Not right or not true.
examples: That answer is wrong.
I took the wrong bus.
You have the wrong shoe.

more.def: Not correct, or not the way something should be.
examples: I got the wrong answer because I added the numbers badly.
She turned the wrong way and got lost in the museum.
Something is wrong with the clock, because it stopped.

easy.def: Bad, and not fair or kind.
examples: It is wrong to take it.
Hurting a pet is wrong.
He knew it was wrong.

more.def: Not good, fair, or honest.
examples: It is wrong to copy someone else's work.
He felt sorry because he knew he had done something wrong.
Telling a lie to a friend is wrong.
